original.reason: It incorrectly applies (iii) to singleton clubs. The condition specifies m positive, so a club of size 1 has no prescribed number of societies. Such clubs contribute student–society incidences omitted from the claimed equality. Indeed, after the full 10001-student club is placed in 5000 societies, one may add any number of further societies, each containing all 10001 singleton clubs; hence k need not equal 5000.

judgment.reason: The double count assumes every club has society multiplicity (|C|-1)/2, which is unjustified for singleton clubs. Its existence construction does not establish uniqueness.
It wrongly applies (iii) to clubs of size 1, so the student–society incidence count can omit singleton-club contributions.
The asserted equality between incidences and pair counts ignores unrestricted singleton clubs; therefore k=5000 is not forced.
